claims.text: The initial Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni eutectic alloy has a continuous, fine lamellar microstructure.
The lamellar microstructure consists of FCC and B2 phases.
The initial inter-lamellar spacing is approximately 2 μm.
The initial alloy has high strength but low room-temperature ductility.
Low ductility in the initial alloy is caused by brittle cracking at lamellar interfaces.
Severe plastic deformation to a true strain greater than 4 followed by a short low-temperature anneal will fragment or globularize the continuous lamellae.
Annealing at 0.4–0.5 Tm, approximately 400–600°C, will cause partial spheroidization without full coarsening.
Deformation at 300–500°C balances work hardening and dynamic recovery.
A strain rate of 10^-2 to 10^-1 s^-1 is an appropriate SPD processing window for producing the proposed structure.
SPD will accumulate a high density of geometrically necessary dislocations at phase interfaces.
The interfacial dislocation density will increase interfacial energy and drive morphological instability of the lamellae.
The subsequent anneal will activate curvature-driven interface migration and dislocation annihilation.
A discontinuous patterned phase configuration will interrupt brittle paths, delocalize strain, and suppress crack nucleation at interfaces.
The patterned microstructure will enable uniform plasticity through grain-boundary sliding and dislocation cross-slip.
The treatment will increase uniform elongation by more than 50% relative to the as-cast state.
The treatment will reduce yield strength by less than 15% relative to the as-cast state.
The failure mode will shift from catastrophic interfacial cracking to ductile void coalescence within the matrix.
The as-cast alloy fractures brittly at strains below 5%.
Success requires dynamic recovery without excessive grain growth or phase decomposition.
The treatment will fail if annealing exceeds a metastable-phase solvus or if deformation strain is insufficient to disrupt lamellar continuity.

contradictions.description: The stated falsification rule labels the result in which SPD produces the predicted ductility increase while HIP produces neither morphological nor ductility improvement as falsifying, even though that result supports the proposed SPD-specific hypothesis. The logical direction of this branch is reversed.
